historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All headline CAGRs (FY2023-FY2026 and FY2021-FY2026) are acquisition-driven (EastMed/DFM FY2023, Hub Aged Care FY2024, ARC Health + Cicada Sept-2025) and none is usable as a driver. Equity CAGR (23-29%) diverges from EPS 3yr (86%) by far more than 30% because FY2023 EPS was depressed by acquisition costs. Organic evidence from H1 FY2027: revenue from operations owned 12+ months grew 8.6% (11.299 vs 10.404), or roughly 5.6% after removing the one month of ARC Health/Cicada that moved into that bucket; ARC ex-acquisitions grew roughly 10%, Community GP fell 2.6%.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner basis (reported FCF less lease principal). SBC is negligible throughout the history, so the gap between reported and owner FCF growth is the lease deduction only, not a dilution signal.

scenario_narratives.base: ARC Medical keeps taking share organically at a high-single-digit to ~10% rate and the July-2026 capitation reweighting, which favours an old, multimorbid enrolled population, sticks; Community GP keeps eroding slowly under its new dedicated manager without a further closure on the scale of Belmont. The H1 FY2027 margin (28.8%) is not fully kept: the flagged step-up in cybersecurity and technology spend and clinician wage pressure take it back to 27-27.5%. No acquisitions are assumed in revenue because none are charged in the flows. Minority partners keep 12.5% of profit.
scenario_narratives.bull: The reweighted capitation formula proves durable through the 2028 formula review and ARC share moves past the ~20% target as the Nurse Practitioner development programme loosens the clinician constraint that has capped facility wins. The Digital Clinical Portal and the decentralised ARC business deliver real operating leverage, taking group EBITDA margin to 30% (ARC already earns 32%), while Community GP stabilises. Growth is fastest in the partly-owned ARC subsidiaries, so minority leakage edges up.
scenario_narratives.bear: Health NZ holds capitation flat in real terms after the FY2027 package, or the aged-care funding-model review (possible from 2027) bundles medical services into ARC-operator payments and TAH becomes a subcontractor on thinner terms. Clinician shortage both caps ARC growth at demographic rates and pushes practitioner cost up faster than funding, taking EBITDA margin from 27% back to 22%, below FY2025's 24.5%. Community GP attrition continues and segment profit, which already halved in H1 FY2027, goes to roughly zero; the cyber spend is permanent. The business stays cash-generative and net cash, so this is a margin case, not a solvency one.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A small, net-cash, asset-light healthcare services business whose history is acquisition-distorted, so the model ignores headline CAGRs and builds attributable owner FCF from components off the trailing twelve months to September 2026: EBITDA, less the full cash lease payment, less 28% tax and a 12.5% minority share, less light capex. Growth is organic only because the flows carry no acquisition spend. Risk is priced in the scenarios (single payer, clinician supply, Community GP decline) and in a 2% size/illiquidity premium, not in stacked discount-rate add-ons. SBC is nil so house and street values coincide.
key_risks_to_valuation: Single payer: capitation and consultation schedules are set by Health NZ; the reweighted formula has its first five-yearly review from 2028 and an aged-care funding-model review could re-route payments through ARC operators.

Margin durability: H1 FY2027's 28.8% EBITDA margin is one half-year after a funding uplift; if wages claw it back to FY2025-FY2026 levels (24.5-25.6%) the base case loses roughly a tenth of its value.
Minority leakage is rising (6.9% to 12.5% of profit in a year) as growth concentrates in the 70-80%-owned ARC subsidiaries; each further point costs about 1% of value.
Discount rate: this build uses 12.5% against the prior 14.5%; the sensitivity grid shows the value at 14.5%.
Community GP: segment profit before tax halved in H1 FY2027 on a 2.6% revenue decline; goodwill and PHO intangibles of 6.3m sit largely against acquisitions in this segment and in ARC.
Liquidity and key-person: ~NZ$38m market cap, thin trading, executive chairman-led, two newly appointed segment managers.
valuation_philosophy.deliberately_unchanged: Scenario weights (25/50/25), base terminal growth (2.75%), the 15% hurdle, lease liabilities excluded from net debt, flat share count, zero SBC. Evidence that would move them: a confirmed funding-model change (weights), a dilutive raise or option grant (share count), an acquisition funded with debt (net debt and growth path).

bridge.note: 2026-11-02 hand-built 5-year model on the FY2026 base, price then 4.06

bridge.item: Methodology: generated 10-year component build, lease charged once (prior deducted lease principal and right-of-use depreciation), one discount rate across scenarios (14.5% vs 13.0/14.5/16.0), Gordon terminal instead of EV/EBITDA exit caps, working-capital capture 15% to 0, organic-only growth paths
bridge.note: residual after the four measured steps; measured at WACC 14.5%, FY2026 anchors, FY2026-level margins, 8.6% NCI

bridge.item: Driver change: EBITDA margin path re-anchored +1.5pt on H1 FY2027 (TTM 27.1% vs FY2026 25.6%)
Anchor refresh: base revenue FY2026 22.488 to TTM Sep-2026 24.702; net cash 1.809 (31 Mar 2026) to 1.939 (30 Sep 2026)
Driver change: minority-interest leakage 8.6% (FY2026) to 12.5% (H1 FY2027), now charged in the flows
Methodology: WACC 14.5% to 12.5% (stacked single-payer, workforce and M&A premia removed; those risks are priced in the bear scenario)

bridge.note: no effect on intrinsic value; upside changes only

inputs.base_revenue_note: Trailing twelve months to 30 Sep 2026 = FY2026 22.488 - H1 FY2026 10.653 + H1 FY2027 12.867. The TTM base is used (not FY2026) so the flows start where the 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet stops; using the FY2026 base with the September balance sheet would count H1 FY2027 cash generation twice. Year 1 is the twelve months to 30 Sep 2027. ARC Health and Cicada Health (acquired 1 Sep 2025) are in the TTM base for all twelve months, so the forward growth path is organic.
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average ordinary shares, H1 FY2027 interim note 13 (9,954k); diluted equals basic, no employee share options outstanding. Held flat: no SBC, no buyback programme, no issuance.
inputs.net_debt_note: Bank loan only (current 0.062 + non-current 0.999 = 1.061) less cash 3.000 = net cash 1.939 at 30 Sep 2026. Lease liabilities (2.346) are excluded because the full lease payment is charged in the flows. The ARC Health / Cicada deferred consideration (0.499) was paid in H1 FY2027, so nothing is outstanding. Cash is consolidated; the small share sitting in 67-80%-owned subsidiaries is not separately disclosed and is not haircut.
inputs.last_fcf_note: TTM reported FCF 4.231 (FY2026 3.830 - H1 FY2026 1.380 + H1 FY2027 1.781) less TTM lease principal 0.343 (0.335 - 0.164 + 0.172, a financing outflow under IFRS 16) less interest income 0.014 less SBC 0. This is a consolidated figure BEFORE the non-controlling share (TTM NCI profit 0.424); the projected flows are attributable-only, see nci_treatment.
inputs.sbc_source: H1 FY2027 interim note 7: share-based payments expense nil (H1 FY2026: -0.036 forfeiture credit); share-based payment reserve nil at 30 Sep 2026; no options outstanding. SBC-zero name: house and street bases coincide.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-18T00:58:53Z (last NZX trade; thinly traded micro-cap, at the 52-week low)
inputs.wacc_rationale: 12.5% in every scenario, built in NZD: NZ 10-year government bond ~4.5% + equity risk premium ~6% at beta ~1.0 = ~10.5%, plus a 2% size/illiquidity premium for a ~NZ$38m market cap with a tightly held register. In line with other NZX micro-caps in this folder (IKE.NZ 12.5%, AGL.NZ 12.0%). The prior build used 13.0/14.5/16.0% (bull/base/bear) with single-payer (+1.0), workforce (+0.5) and M&A/minority (+0.5) premia stacked on top; those three risks are exactly what the bear scenario's growth and margin paths price, and the NCI is now charged in the flows, so they are removed from the rate and the rate no longer differs by scenario (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment B, leases as an operating cost: the full cash lease payment (principal + interest; H1 FY2027 0.259 = 2.0% of revenue, FY2026 0.506 = 2.25%) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path, and lease liabilities (2.346) are excluded from net debt. D&A in the tax build excludes right-of-use depreciation. The prior build deducted lease principal AND a 4.5%-of-revenue D&A that included right-of-use depreciation, charging the lease twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows; nothing deducted in the bridge. Non-controlling interests (Hub Aged Care 70%-owned, ARC Health 80%, Cicada Health 70%, EastMed 67%) took 12.5% of group profit in H1 FY2027 (0.263 of 2.104), up from 6.9% in H1 FY2026 and 8.6% in FY2026 as the Sept-2025 acquisitions contributed a full half. That 12.5% leakage is folded into cash_tax_rate_path: 1 - (1 - 0.28) x (1 - 0.125) = 37.0%. Calibration: TTM EBITDA 6.688 - lease cash 0.514 - deductible D&A 0.15 = EBIT 6.02; x 0.63 = 3.79 attributable NOPAT, against TTM attributable net income 3.251 + the parent's share of non-deductible acquisition amortisation ~0.53 + after-tax bank and deferred-consideration interest ~0.09 = 3.87. Ties within 2%.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the non-US adaptations (leases, NCI, SBC-zero). An asset-light operating company (managed GP/NP services to aged residential care plus a smaller community GP business) whose value is a free-cash-flow stream; not a bank, REIT or holdco. Same model family as the prior valuation, migrated from a hand-built 5-year JSON to the generated 10-year Drivers route. cash_tax_rate_path is a COMBINED 28% NZ company tax and 12.5% minority-interest leakage, not a tax rate. da_pct_path carries only tax-deductible D&A (PP&E depreciation and software amortisation, 0.078 in H1 FY2027 = 0.6% of revenue): right-of-use depreciation is replaced by the lease charge, and amortisation of acquired PHO-contract intangibles (0.320 in H1 FY2027) is non-cash and not deductible, which is why TTM cash tax ties to 28% of EBIT before that amortisation (modelled 1.69 vs current tax ~1.68). Growth is organic only: the flows carry no acquisition spend, so no bolt-on revenue is assumed. SBC is nil, so the house/street band collapses to a point. Interest income (0.014 TTM) is immaterial and net cash is under 1x FCF. Dividend is a fixed 4.0 cents per quarter fully imputed (16 cps); the Q2 interim declared after balance date (0.398) is an ordinary distribution and not adjusted. No buybacks; the flat share count is real, not a convention.

base.growth_rationale: Organic only. ARC (71% of revenue) growing ~10% ex-acquisitions with nine more months of the 1 July 2026 capitation uplift (6.32% base plus the age/multimorbidity reweighting) still to annualise; Community GP (29%) shrinking ~2-3%. Blended 7.5% in year 1, fading to 3% as ARC share gains toward management's ~20% target saturate and growth converges on demographics plus funding indexation.
base.margin_rationale: TTM EBITDA margin 27.1%; H1 FY2027 28.8% against 25.9% in H1 FY2026 and 25.2% in H2 FY2026. The step-up is the capitation reweighting dropping through in ARC (segment EBITDA margin 26.0% to 32.4%) partly offset by Community GP (25.6% to 19.8%). Year 1 is set at 27.5%, below the H1 run-rate, for the cybersecurity/technology spend the Chairman flagged ('accepting some cost to short-term earnings') and clinician wage catch-up; 27.0% long run, since single-payer pricing gains have historically been shared with the workforce.
base.wc_rationale: Zero. No deferred-revenue model; working capital was a 0.08 inflow in FY2026 and roughly a 0.44 outflow in H1 FY2027 (receivables +0.6 on consultation billing growth). The prior build's +15% capture is not supported by either period.

bull.tax_rationale: 37.5%: the partly-owned ARC subsidiaries outgrow the wholly-owned businesses in this path, lifting NCI leakage to ~13%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Unchanged from the prior build. Bear 25% rather than the 15% house default because effectively all revenue comes from one payer (Health NZ via PHOs) and a funding-model review is live. Base 50%: the H1 FY2027 print confirms the capitation uplift is flowing and ARC is growing organically. Bull 25% rather than 35% because it needs three independent things at once: durable funding, a loosened clinician supply and a stabilised Community GP.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
